theory.intro: A table of values has two rows. The rule tells you how to get the bottom row from the top row.
facts: For a multiplicative rule, **divide** a bottom value by the matching top value to find the multiplier.
The same multiplier should work for **every** column.
Write the rule as 'bottom $= n \times$ top'.
steps: Pick one column and divide the bottom number by the top number.
Check that this multiplier works for the other columns.
State the rule connecting the two rows.

foundation.question_text: Determine the rule connecting the rows: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&1&2&5\\\hline\text{Bottom}&4&8&20\end{array}$.
What rule maps the top row to the bottom row? $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&2&3&6\\\hline\text{Bottom}&10&15&30\end{array}$.

development.question_text: Find and check the rule for $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&4&7&12\\\hline\text{Bottom}&52&91&156\end{array}$.
Find the rule and use it to fill the blank: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&5&9&14\\\hline\text{Bottom}&95&171&\square\end{array}$.
Find the rule and the missing top value: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&4&\square&12\\\hline\text{Bottom}&92&161&276\end{array}$.
Does one multiplication rule fit every column? If so, state it: $\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Top}&6&9&13\\\hline\text{Bottom}&174&261&377\end{array}$.
A rule maps top to bottom. Find it and evaluate the bottom value when the top is $16$: $\begin{array}{c|cc}\text{Top}&3&7\\\hline\text{Bottom}&93&217\end{array}$.

mastery.question_text: One entry is wrong: $\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Top}&4&6&9&12\\\hline\text{Bottom}&148&222&333&440\end{array}$. Determine the intended multiplication rule and correct the entry.
The first column of a table is $(5,215)$. A second column is $(8,344)$. Find the multiplication rule and the top value paired with $559$.
Kai claims the rule for pairs $(7,329)$, $(10,470)$ and $(14,658)$ is bottom $=46 \times$ top. Test the claim and give the correct rule.
mastery.solution_text:
$329 \div 7=47$
$470 \div 10=47$
$658 \div 14=47$
Kai's claim is false. Bottom $=47 \times$ top.
